Execution or drop of fake AI-platform installer (DeepSeek/Manus/Seedance/GPT-5.5/Kimi) AIInstallation High
Detects the malicious installer binaries Storm-3075 ships through SEO-poisoned GitHub repos masquerading as AI tools (DeepSeek-V4, Manus AI, Seedance, GPT-5.5, Kimi-Swarm). Combines verbatim filename match, the eight MSTI-published SHA256 hashes, and a permissive regex pattern keyed on the consistent '*_x64.exe' naming convention dropped into Downloads/Temp. Rationale: Three layers of fidelity: (1) verbatim FileName match for the seven binaries enumerated in MSTI's lure-table (rows 2-6); (2) hash-equal on all eight published SHA256 IOCs — zero-FP even if the file is renamed; (3) regex on the campaign's consistent '*_x64.exe' naming convention scoped to Downloads/Temp/Public to catch future siblings dropped from the same MSaaS signing pipeline. Article explicitly notes Storm-3075 uses these names through fake GitHub orgs (DeepSeek-V4, ManusAI-agent, bytedance-seedance).
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1608.005 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate DeepSeek / ByteDance Seedance / Moonshot Kimi installer downloaded from the official vendor site (distinguishable via publisher cert: vendor-signed not MSaaS-signed)
  • Security researcher detonating samples in a corp-attached sandbox VM
  • IT redistributing the genuine open-source AI model launcher to dev workstations
  • Renamed in-house tool that accidentally matches the naming regex (e.g. 'kimi-swarm-station' if your firm runs an internal swarm orchestrator)
  • Threat-hunting team replaying historical IOCs as part of detection-engineering validation
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\\\<dfs-share>\\\\Software\\\\")) and DeviceName !in~ ("<sandbox-host-list>")
Response runbook
Triage: pull SHA256 + publisher cert details for the matching ProcessId; if hash is on the MSTI list, treat as confirmed Storm-3075. Check ParentImage — Downloads-folder browser parent confirms SEO-poisoning vector; cmd/PowerShell parent suggests script-stage. Contain: isolate the host via Defender LiveResponse, kill the process, hash-block the SHA256 tenant-wide in Defender Indicators, revoke the user's Azure AD refresh tokens. Hunt: look for the same SHA256 / FileName across the whole estate (DeviceFileEvents), pivot DeviceNetworkEvents on the affected host to the IOC domains in UC3 for the past 30 days, and review the user's browser history / EmailUrlInfo for the GitHub-repo SEO landing.
let lure_binaries = dynamic(["deepseek-v4-pro_x64.exe","deepseek-v4-flash_x64.exe","Manus_AI_Desktop_x64.exe","seedance_x64.exe","gpt-5.5-Pro_x64.exe","gpt-5.5-Thinking_x64.exe","Kimi-Swarm-Station_x64.exe"]);
let ioc_sha256 = dynamic(["791efb555eefb7215e96659a1353a97416743b66bdd72705493129c64057d40e","c7c5072df9f83f4c440a5c3bb4be1d5f6c67bbf78f196406ca20d27b43b975b8","0a26238f6c516de5885457c93042531aa59bc206a9537cebf5267cedc6c68531","8610d4fb0ec5b525071c2aaec4df0f8fcbb3673aba58a7e1959fc44e83c0e2ca","99231deb373997364381d1eb513d2d42231d418c3a2db9007c5af9bd56ab9371","25270cc429ada8028b5b33220ed412c47907ecceea7377d608fac5af01bed56a","56d722b0331bf0aaa86bb37483486c6dff6ad9427fc473ed7c3226c21a9bdd23","5455341ed1bbe75a664fca2dd0794c508e1874f75360253a7ff5bc119bc92d80"]);
let ai_lure_regex = @"(?i)^(deepseek-v\d+(-pro|-flash)?|manus_ai_desktop|seedance|gpt-\d+(\.\d+)?-(pro|thinking)|kimi-swarm-station)_x64\.exe$";
union isfuzzy=false
    (DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
        | where FileName in~ (lure_binaries)
            or SHA256 in (ioc_sha256)
            or (FileName matches regex ai_lure_regex and FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\",@"\Temp\",@"\AppData\Local\Temp\",@"\Public\"))
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, EvtKind = "process", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
    (DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
        | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
        | where FileName in~ (lure_binaries) or SHA256 in (ioc_sha256)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, EvtKind = "file", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessParentFileName)
| order by Timestamp desc
let lure_binaries = dynamic(["deepseek-v4-pro_x64.exe","deepseek-v4-flash_x64.exe","Manus_AI_Desktop_x64.exe","seedance_x64.exe","gpt-5.5-Pro_x64.exe","gpt-5.5-Thinking_x64.exe","Kimi-Swarm-Station_x64.exe"]);
let ioc_sha256 = dynamic(["791efb555eefb7215e96659a1353a97416743b66bdd72705493129c64057d40e","c7c5072df9f83f4c440a5c3bb4be1d5f6c67bbf78f196406ca20d27b43b975b8","0a26238f6c516de5885457c93042531aa59bc206a9537cebf5267cedc6c68531","8610d4fb0ec5b525071c2aaec4df0f8fcbb3673aba58a7e1959fc44e83c0e2ca","99231deb373997364381d1eb513d2d42231d418c3a2db9007c5af9bd56ab9371","25270cc429ada8028b5b33220ed412c47907ecceea7377d608fac5af01bed56a","56d722b0331bf0aaa86bb37483486c6dff6ad9427fc473ed7c3226c21a9bdd23","5455341ed1bbe75a664fca2dd0794c508e1874f75360253a7ff5bc119bc92d80"]);
let ai_lure_regex = @"(?i)(deepseek-v\d+(-pro|-flash)?|manus_ai_desktop|seedance|gpt-\d+(\.\d+)?-(pro|thinking)|kimi-swarm-station)_x64\.exe";
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
        | where tolower(ActingProcessName) has_any (lure_binaries)
            or SHA256 in (ioc_sha256)
            or ActingProcessName matches regex ai_lure_regex
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EvtKind="process", ActingProcessName, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256),

Phishing redirect chain via awstrack.me / Rebrandly into AI-themed landing path AIDelivery Medium
Detects user clicks on the multi-hop redirect chain Storm-3075/affiliates use to launder phish URLs: legit CRM (bitrix24) → Amazon awstrack.me email-tracking → Rebrandly short link → compromised legendarytrendsbay[.]shop /ChatGPT/ path (or sibling AI-themed paths). Targets the SHAPE of the chain (awstrack.me forwarding into an AI-brand path), not just static IOCs, so it also catches campaign rotation. Rationale: Two pivot shapes from the MSTI ChatGPT-phish attack chain: (1) literal IOC match on the six known phish landings; (2) behavioural pattern of a click through awstrack.me/Rebrandly/bitrix24 that terminates at a path containing an AI-brand token — this is the exact funnel diagrammed in Figure 1 and survives URL rotation since the AI-brand path component is the lure invariant. Path-regex /(ChatGPT|Claude|Anthropic|DeepSeek)/ also catches the article's note that the threat actor placed phishing pages in a /ChatGPT/ folder on compromised legendarytrendsbay[.]shop.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1102 T1656
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Marketing or sales team using Bitrix24 CRM legitimately, with AWS SES tracking and an AI-themed campaign name in the URL
  • Legitimate Anthropic / OpenAI newsletter using Rebrandly short links (verify the terminal landing is the genuine vendor domain)
  • Security awareness training that simulates this exact lure (Defender Attack Simulator may surface here)
  • Procurement team evaluating an AI vendor demo via a shortened URL containing the vendor name
  • Internal employee blog post embedding a Rebrandly link that references an AI tool
Suppression filter
and AccountUpn !in~ ("<known-marketing-accounts>") and not (UrlChain has "openai.com" or UrlChain has "anthropic.com" or UrlChain has "deepseek.com")
Response runbook
Triage: inspect the full UrlChain field — confirm the chain terminates at a non-vendor domain (legendarytrendsbay[.]shop, awaydouble[.]org, etc.) not openai.com / anthropic.com / deepseek.com. Pull EmailUrlInfo by the matching NetworkMessageId to identify the originating phish. Contain: revoke active sessions for the AccountUpn via Entra ID risky-user workflow; add Conditional Access requirement for re-MFA on next sign-in; block the terminal landing domain at proxy. Hunt: SigninLogs for the same UPN looking for unfamiliar-location or device-not-compliant sign-ins in the click + 4h window (AiTM token theft); EmailEvents for siblings of the same campaign that hit other recipients.
let phish_landings = dynamic(["legendarytrendsbay.shop","dash.awaydouble.org","awaydouble.org","servicing.pureplantcravings.com","pureplantcravings.com","brokeapt.com"]);
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")

    or Url matches regex @"(?i)https?://[^/]+/(ChatGPT|Claude|Anthropic|DeepSeek)/"
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlChain, ActionType, IsClickedThrough, IPAddress, Workload
| order by Timestamp desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["791efb555eefb7215e96659a1353a97416743b66bdd72705493129c64057d40e", "c7c5072df9f83f4c440a5c3bb4be1d5f6c67bbf78f196406ca20d27b43b975b8", "0a26238f6c516de5885457c93042531aa59bc206a9537cebf5267cedc6c68531", "8610d4fb0ec5b525071c2aaec4df0f8fcbb3673aba58a7e1959fc44e83c0e2ca", "99231deb373997364381d1eb513d2d42231d418c3a2db9007c5af9bd56ab9371", "25270cc429ada8028b5b33220ed412c47907ecceea7377d608fac5af01bed56a", "56d722b0331bf0aaa86bb37483486c6dff6ad9427fc473ed7c3226c21a9bdd23", "5455341ed1bbe75a664fca2dd0794c508e1874f75360253a7ff5bc119bc92d80", "4f5c5b3ef45cfff7721754487a86aeff9a2e6e32", "fbfe7513685913e6f878647eec429d45", "562d48524313d414b5a419fed6ca10aa", "b96c0d609c1b7e74f8cb1442bf0b5418", "dbaa133fd3d1a834460206d83b480f80", "22c0c7d441fd22432cfe7854b59ba82b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |

    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] CVE-2026-47430 fleet exposure via Defender TVM (vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser install on dev endpoint (CVE-2026-47430)

Vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser install on dev endpoint (CVE-2026-47430) AIWeaponization Medium
Hunts for npm / yarn / pnpm / cordova-cli invocations that install cordova-plugin-inappbrowser at a version <6.0.1, the range vulnerable to arbitrary Cordova callback dispatch from InAppBrowser WebView content (CDVWKInAppBrowser.m:560–574). Catches the moment the vulnerable iOS Cordova plugin enters a developer's workspace so the org can patch BEFORE the iOS build ships. Rationale: Article names the exact npm package (`cordova-plugin-inappbrowser`) and the precise vulnerable range (3.1.0 through 6.0.0, fixed 6.0.1). The detection ties the CLI invocations that introduce the package to a version-pin regex covering all vulnerable majors plus the explicit `6.0.0` boundary, and excludes the `6.0.1+` safe pins and non-installing subcommands (uninstall/list). Cross-checked the GHSA URL in the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q42j-x8rq-pjg6
ATT&CKT1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer intentionally pinning to an older version for compatibility testing against legacy cordova-ios
  • Security researcher reproducing CVE-2026-47430 in a sandbox repo
  • CI/CD build agent restoring a legacy package-lock.json that still references 5.x
  • Plugin documentation / `npm view cordova-plugin-inappbrowser` lookups that happen to mention the name
  • Cordova app vendor that has not yet released a 6.0.1-compatible build and pins the last known good version internally
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service") and not (ProcessCommandLine has_any (" uninstall"," remove "," rm "," list "," ls "," view "," info "," search "))
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the affected repo, confirm the install was real (compare the package.json / package-lock.json / config.xml delta against the prior commit, not just the CLI history) and verify the host app actually targets iOS via cordova-ios — Android-only builds aren't exposed by this CVE. 2) Contain: open a PR to bump cordova-plugin-inappbrowser to >=6.0.1, rebuild and re-publish any TestFlight / App Store / enterprise-distribution builds, and where the affected app handles OAuth or session tokens, rotate refresh tokens issued to the prior app version. 3) Hunt: enumerate every repo, CI cache, and developer workspace in the org for cordova-plugin-inappbrowser <6.0.1, push a bulk Dependabot/Renovate update, then for each affected iOS app, check production sign-in / token-issuance logs for the prior 60 days for anomalous Cordova plugin callback patterns (rapid sequential refreshes, mismatched user-agent vs. token issuance).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","cordova.cmd","cordova.exe","ionic.cmd","node.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "cordova-plugin-inappbrowser"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (" install"," add"," plugin add"," i ","--save"," -S")
| extend PinnedVersion = extract(@"cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| where isempty(PinnedVersion) or PinnedVersion matches regex @"^(3\.|4\.|5\.|6\.0\.0$)"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any (" uninstall"," remove "," rm "," list "," ls "," view "))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, PinnedVersion
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(npm|npx|yarn|pnpm|cordova|ionic|node)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$"
| where CommandLine has "cordova-plugin-inappbrowser"
| where CommandLine has_any (" install"," add"," plugin add"," i ","--save"," -S")
| extend PinnedVersion = extract(@"cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)", 1, CommandLine)
| where isempty(PinnedVersion) or PinnedVersion matches regex @"^(3\.|4\.|5\.|6\.0\.0$)"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where not (CommandLine has_any (" uninstall"," remove "," rm "," list "," ls "," view "))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, PinnedVersion
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser install (CVE-2026-47430)
id: 8e6c4b8a-3d2a-4e6f-9d7b-1c0e2a4b8d6a
description: |
  Detects npm / yarn / pnpm / cordova / ionic CLI invocations that install
  cordova-plugin-inappbrowser in a version range vulnerable to CVE-2026-47430
  (3.1.0 through 6.0.0). Pinned safe versions (>=6.0.1) are excluded.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q42j-x8rq-pjg6
author: Detection engineering
date: 2026/06/14
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.001
  - cve.2026.47430
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\npx.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\cordova.cmd'
      - '\cordova.exe'
      - '\ionic.cmd'
      - '\node.exe'
  selection_pkg:
    CommandLine|contains: 'cordova-plugin-inappbrowser'
  selection_action:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' install'
      - ' add'
      - ' plugin add'
  filter_safe_pin:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@6.0.1'
      - 'cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@6.0.2'
      - 'cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@6.1'
      - 'cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@7'
  filter_uninstall:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' uninstall'
      - ' remove '
      - ' rm '
      - ' list '
      - ' ls '
  condition: selection_proc and selection_pkg and selection_action and not (filter_safe_pin or filter_uninstall)
level: medium
falsepositives:
  - Developer intentionally pinning to a still-vulnerable version for compatibility testing
  - Security researcher reproducing the CVE in a sandbox repo
  - CI agent restoring a legacy package-lock.json that still references 5.x
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\YARN.EXE OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\cordova.cmd OR *\\cordova.exe OR *\\CORDOVA.EXE OR *\\ionic.cmd OR *\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE)) @CommandLine:*cordova-plugin-inappbrowser* (@CommandLine:*install* OR @CommandLine:*add*) -@CommandLine:*cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@6.0.1* -@CommandLine:*cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@6.0.2* -@CommandLine:*cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@6.1* -@CommandLine:*uninstall*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(npm|npx|yarn|pnpm|cordova|ionic|node)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$/i CommandLine=/cordova-plugin-inappbrowser/i
| regex("\\b(install|add|plugin\\s+add)\\b", field=CommandLine)
| NOT CommandLine=/cordova-plugin-inappbrowser@(6\.0\.[1-9]|6\.[1-9]|[7-9]\.)/i
| NOT CommandLine=/(uninstall|\sremove\s|\srm\s|\slist\s|\sls\s)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
CVE-2026-47430 fleet exposure via Defender TVM (vulnerable cordova-plugin-inappbrowser) AIReconnaissance High
Direct CVE-keyed asset-discovery hunt against Defender Threat & Vulnerability Management for every device the scanner has tagged as carrying CVE-2026-47430. Drives patch prioritisation for iOS Cordova apps whose host plugin (cordova-plugin-inappbrowser) sits below 6.0.1 and is exploitable via attacker-controlled WebView content. Rationale: The advisory ships CVE-2026-47430 against npm:cordova-plugin-inappbrowser <6.0.1. A direct CveId match against the Defender TVM tables is the cleanest, lowest-FP fleet-exposure inventory — it pivots on the article's primary identifier with no need to model the exploit chain itself. The detection has no FP risk from process-level noise because TVM only flags hosts where the scanner actually identified the affected SoftwareVersion. Cross-checked GHSA URL. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q42j-x8rq-pjg6
ATT&CKT1592.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TVM scan lag — host already patched but inventory not yet rescanned post-bump
  • Developer workstation with two checkout copies of the same repo (counted twice)
  • Build host with the vulnerable plugin cached under a non-active workspace but no longer used
  • Test fixture intentionally pinned to vulnerable version for the project's own CVE regression suite
  • Defender TVM may not natively map every npm-package CVE — coverage gaps yield false negatives rather than false positives, but means an empty result is not conclusive on its own
Response runbook
1) Triage: per device hit, pull the SoftwareName and SoftwareVersion and verify with a manual `npm ls cordova-plugin-inappbrowser` (or grep the affected workspace's package-lock.json) to rule out stale TVM telemetry. 2) Contain: drive each affected developer / build host to upgrade the plugin to >=6.0.1, rebuild any iOS Cordova app that bundled the old version, and pull / revoke any external TestFlight or App Store builds that shipped a vulnerable bundle. 3) Hunt: cross-reference the affected hostnames against MDM and iOS app-inventory to identify which production user-facing apps actually embedded the vulnerable plugin, then in those apps' identity logs (sign-in, OAuth consent, token refresh) look back 60 days for anomalous behaviour consistent with attacker-driven callback spoofing — unexpected camera/contacts/file plugin invocations from app sessions that opened external URLs in InAppBrowser, or token-refresh storms from a single device.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-47430"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            ObservedVersions = make_set(SoftwareVersion),
            Severity = any(VulnerabilitySeverityLevel),
            RecommendedFix = any(RecommendedSecurityUpdate)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName
| order by LastSeen desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-47430"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            ObservedVersions = make_set(SoftwareVersion),
            Severity = any(VulnerabilitySeverityLevel),
            RecommendedFix = any(RecommendedSecurityUpdate)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName
| order by LastSeen desc
APPLICATION
search index=defender_tvm sourcetype="defender:tvm:vulnerabilities" CveId="CVE-2026-47430"
| stats min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(SoftwareVersion) as observed_versions values(VulnerabilitySeverityLevel) as severity by DeviceName SoftwareVendor SoftwareName
| convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
| sort - last_seen

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental

    product: windows

        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'

        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] HTTP access to Shopper admin team-settings / Livewire endpoints (CVE-2026-47744)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
HTTP access to Shopper admin team-settings / Livewire endpoints (CVE-2026-47744) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts HTTP requests to the vulnerable Shopper admin panel routes — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — including their Livewire AJAX endpoints. Pre-patch (Shopper < 2.8.0) these were reachable by any authenticated panel user and were the only network observable for the authorization-bypass / RBAC privilege-escalation chain disclosed in GHSA-c3qp-2ggw-xjg7. Rationale: The article names exactly two Livewire components — Settings/Team/Index and Settings/Team/RolePermission — as the abuse surface. Livewire routes those component names verbatim through /livewire/update (Livewire v3) and /livewire/message/{component} (v2), so the component string and these endpoints are the highest-fidelity strings available pre-exploit. POST/PUT/PATCH on the role-permission route is the specific action that grants/escalates permissions, distinguishing exploitation from normal page loads. No external IOC corroboration was attempted since the advisory exposes no network IOCs — only source-code paths.
ATT&CKT1190 T1068 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Shopper panel administrators (manage_users holders) creating roles or updating role permissions in normal operations
  • Internal QA / penetration-test exercises against the upgraded (>=2.8.0) panel
  • Application monitoring/uptime probes hitting the admin panel index without authentication (will 302 to login but still appear in HTTP logs)
  • Crawlers / bots probing /livewire/update on any Livewire-built site (broad Livewire scanners)
  • Reverse-proxy retries duplicating the same POST to /livewire/update on transient 5xx
Suppression filter
| where not (User in~ ("admin","superadmin") and ClientIP in ("10.0.0.0/8","192.168.0.0/16")) and not (UserAgent has_any ("Pingdom","UptimeRobot","StatusCake"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the Shopper composer.lock from the affected host and confirm shopper/framework < 2.8.0; if patched, downgrade severity. Identify the authenticated session behind the request (panel session cookie or X-Forwarded-User) and map to the panel user — was it a holder of view_users only? 2) Contain: force-logout all panel sessions, rotate panel admin credentials, and either upgrade to shopper/framework 2.8.0 immediately or block /livewire/update and /admin/settings/team* at the WAF until upgrade. 3) Hunt: dump the roles and role_permission tables and diff against a known-good snapshot — look for newly granted manage_users / edit_orders to non-admin accounts; review the panel users table for unexpected deletions of legitimate administrators; pivot on the source IP across the prior 30 days for any other panel reconnaissance.
// Requires IIS / nginx access logs ingested to a custom table; M365 Defender XDR does not natively capture inbound HTTP to a self-hosted PHP app.
// Pivot via DeviceNetworkEvents for the web server's inbound traffic to the panel's listening port, then triage in the proxy/WAF.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where LocalPort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm.exe","php.exe","nginx.exe","httpd.exe","caddy.exe")
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| summarize Connections = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where Connections > 5
| order by LastSeen desc
let TargetPaths = dynamic(["settings/team","settings.team.index","settings.team.role-permission","settings.team.rolepermission","/livewire/update","/livewire/message/settings.team"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where csUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or csUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Computer, Method=csMethod, Url=strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Status=scStatus, ClientIP=cIP, UserAgent=csUserAgent, User=csUserName),
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where CsUriStem has_any (TargetPaths) or CsUriQuery has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="AppService", Computer=CsHost, Method=CsMethod, Url=strcat(CsUriStem, iff(isnotempty(CsUriQuery), strcat("?", CsUriQuery), "")), Status=ScStatus, ClientIP=CIp, UserAgent=UserAgent, User=CsUsername),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where RequestURL has_any (TargetPaths)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source=DeviceProduct, Computer=DestinationHostName, Method=RequestMethod, Url=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), ClientIP=SourceIP, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, User=SourceUserName)
)
| where Method in~ ("POST","PUT","PATCH") or Url has_any ("role-permission","rolepermission")
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Methods = make_set(Method), Statuses = make_set(Status), UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 5), Users = make_set(User, 10) by ClientIP, Computer, Source
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Shopper Admin Team Settings / Livewire Endpoint Access (CVE-2026-47744)
id: 9f6c5d22-2e4f-4b3a-9d6e-7c8a2b9d4e10
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP requests to Shopper admin panel team-settings routes (Settings/Team/Index, Settings/Team/RolePermission) and their underlying Livewire endpoints, which were the abuse path for CVE-2026-47744 (authorization bypass + RBAC privilege escalation) in shopper/framework versions below 2.8.0.
references:
    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c3qp-2ggw-xjg7
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1190
    - attack.t1068
    - attack.t1078.003
    - cve.2026.47744
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection_path:
        cs-uri-stem|contains:
            - 'settings/team'
            - 'settings.team.index'
            - 'settings.team.role-permission'
            - 'settings.team.rolepermission'
            - '/livewire/update'
            - '/livewire/message/settings.team'
    condition: selection_path
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate Shopper administrators managing roles in the admin panel
    - Internal QA/staging exercising the team settings page
level: medium
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:iis OR source:azure.app_services) (@http.url_details.path:(*settings/team* OR *settings.team.index* OR *settings.team.role-permission* OR *settings.team.rolePermission*) OR @http.url_details.path:(*/livewire/update* OR */livewire/message/settings.team*)) AND @http.method:(POST OR PUT OR PATCH)
# log group: /aws/applicationelb (or /aws/cloudfront/access-logs, /aws/wafv2) — point at whichever fronts the Shopper admin panel
fields @timestamp, request_url, request_verb, elb_status_code, client_ip, user_agent, target_processing_time
| filter (request_url like /settings\/team/ 
         or request_url like /settings\.team\.index/ 
         or request_url like /settings\.team\.role-?permission/i
         or request_url like /\/livewire\/(update|message\/settings\.team)/)
      and request_verb in ["POST","PUT","PATCH"]
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.http_method) as http_method values(Web.status) as status values(Web.user) as user values(Web.src) as src_ip values(Web.url) as url from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url IN ("*settings/team*","*settings.team.index*","*settings.team.role-permission*","*settings.team.rolePermission*") OR Web.url IN ("*/livewire/update*","*/livewire/message/settings.team*")) by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.http_method Web.status Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where http_method IN ("POST","PUT","PATCH") OR like(url,"%role-permission%") | sort 0 - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.http_method) as http_method values(Web.status) as status values(Web.user) as user values(Web.src) as src_ip values(Web.url) as url from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url IN ("*settings/team*","*settings.team.index*","*settings.team.role-permission*","*settings.team.rolePermission*") OR Web.url IN ("*/livewire/update*","*/livewire/message/settings.team*")) by Web.src Web.user Web.url Web.http_method Web.status Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where http_method IN ("POST","PUT","PATCH") OR like(url,"%role-permission%") | sort 0 - lastTime

| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

2026-06-05 4 use cases 1 technique 3 kill-chain phases detected

NASA AMMOS Instrument Toolkit: Path traversal resulting in arbitrary file append (can be triggered over the network by unauthenticated attacker)

CVEsCVE-2026-47731
ATT&CKT1190

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Unauthenticated POST to AIT-BSC /<name>/start with path-traversal form fields (CVE-2026-47731) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-47731: NASA AMMOS Instrument Toolkit: Path traversal

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Unauthenticated POST to AIT-BSC /<name>/start with path-traversal form fields (CVE-2026-47731) AIExploitation High
Hunts the actual exploit shape against the AIT-Core BSC HTTP API: POST to /<name>/start carrying attacker-controlled log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, or path form fields with path-traversal indicators (../, %2e%2e, absolute paths like /etc, /home, /root). Pre-patch AIT-Core <3.1.1 and <2.6.1 lets an unauthenticated remote caller use these fields to redirect log_file writes anywhere ait-bsc can write — corruption of .py modules then yields RCE on next restart. Rationale: Targets the exact REST shape from the article (the Bottle route `/<name>/start` registered in `StreamCaptureManagerServer._route()`) plus the three attacker-influenced form fields named in the bug write-up (log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, path) combined with traversal markers (../ %2e%2e absolute /etc /root /home). The article confirms there is no auth on the route and these fields go straight into `os.path.join` without realpath canonicalisation. Cross-checked against the GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 advisory and the AIT-Core 3.1.1/2.6.1 patch notes which scope the same parameter list. Falcon FDR doesn't natively ship HTTP request bodies so falcon_logscale_query is empty; the same telemetry is covered by NetworkConnectIP4 in UC2. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/releases/tag/3.1.1
ATT&CKT1190 T1565.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Burp Pro) probing the BSC endpoint as part of a sanctioned scan
  • Mission-ops engineers running `python_poc.py` from the AIT-Core test harness against a lab BSC instance
  • Custom ground-system tooling that legitimately passes log_dir_path to relocate captures between mission phases
  • Health-check probes that POST malformed bodies to /start to verify the route is alive (yields 400 but trips URL pattern)
Suppression filter
and not (SrcIp in ("10.", "172.16.", "192.168.") and UA has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Tenable","Burp","Acunetix","Nmap")) and not (Uri endswith "/healthcheck/start")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full POST body from the proxy/WAF capture, decode the form fields, and verify whether log_dir_path / path resolves outside the configured `root_log_directory` from bsc.yaml. Pivot on `source IP` to see whether the same caller hit /stats or other handler names. Contain: block the source IP at the perimeter and stop the ait-bsc systemd unit (`systemctl stop ait-bsc`) — do NOT just kill the process because gevent greenlets can keep writing in an infinite-loop bug mentioned in the advisory. Hunt: review DeviceFileEvents for writes by python/ait-bsc into /etc, /root, /home/*/.ssh, site-packages/ait/, or any *.py outside the project tree in the previous 24h; verify SHA256 of any AIT-Core .py against the package wheel hashes; check for outbound TCP from ait-bsc to non-baseline destinations (see related UC2).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionFound","ListeningConnectionCreated")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(python(3(\.\d+)?)?|ait-bsc)(\.exe)?$"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ait-bsc","ait.core.bsc","ait_bsc","StreamCaptureManagerServer","bsc.yaml")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Sessions=count(), AnyLocalPort=any(LocalPort) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let TraversalTokens = dynamic(["log_dir_path","file_name_pattern","..%2F","..%2f","..%5C","..%5c","%2e%2e","path=%2F","path=/etc","path=/root","path=/home","path=/var","path=/tmp","log_dir_path=/"]);
let IISHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)^/[^/]+/start$"
    | where csUriQuery has_any (TraversalTokens) or csUriStem has_any ("%2e%2e", "..")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=tostring(cIP), DstPort=tostring(sPort), Uri=csUriStem, Detail=csUriQuery, UA=csUserAgent, Source="W3CIIS";
let CEFHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
    | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)/[^/]+/start(\?|$)"
    | where Message has_any (TraversalTokens) or RequestURL has_any ("%2e%2e", "..")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, DeviceExternalID), SrcIp=SourceIP, DstPort=tostring(DestinationPort), Uri=RequestURL, Detail=Message, UA=RequestClientApplication, Source="CEF";
let SyslogHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ProcessName has_any ("ait-bsc","ait_bsc","bsc","python","python3")
    | where SyslogMessage has "/start" and SyslogMessage has_any (TraversalTokens)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=HostIP, DstPort="", Uri="/<name>/start", Detail=SyslogMessage, UA="", Source="Syslog";
union IISHits, CEFHits, SyslogHits
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count(), SampleDetail=any(Detail) by Host, SrcIp, Uri, Source
| order by LastSeen desc

ait-bsc outbound TCP to public/non-baseline destination (attacker-supplied loc port) AICommand & Control High
Detects ait-bsc / python processes running the ait.core.bsc StreamCaptureManager opening outbound TCP/UDP sessions to non-RFC1918, non-baseline destinations. Per CVE-2026-47731 the unauth /<name>/start endpoint lets a remote caller supply arbitrary `loc` + `port` form values which BSC dutifully `gevent.spawn`s a socket against — making BSC initiate egress to attacker-controlled infrastructure that then streams attacker-chosen bytes back into the file append sink. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article-confirmed primitive: the attacker controls `loc` and `port` in the form body and BSC `gevent.spawn`s a SocketStreamCapturer at that endpoint — i.e. BSC initiates the egress under attacker direction. Process-context match uses the exact module path (`ait.core.bsc`), class name (`StreamCaptureManagerServer`), and config file (`bsc.yaml`) shown in the source excerpt. Sentinel query splits process-context resolution onto ImProcessCreate (which carries ActingProcessCommandLine) and joins by DvcHostname into ImNetworkSession (which does not) — the schema-correct way to express the same logic the Defender query expresses inline. Cross-checked against GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 patch diff which restricts socket creation to validated paths only. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p462-prxw-mjx4 • https://github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Core/blob/main/ait/core/bsc.py
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1659
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate ground-station configurations where BSC connects to a public-IP downlink receiver (rare, but check bsc.yaml first)
  • Mission-ops sites running ait-bsc against a cloud-hosted relay (AWS Ground Station, Azure Orbital) which presents as a public IP
  • Engineer testing against a remote development BSC server over a tunnel that egresses to the tunnel endpoint's public IP
  • Updates / pip installs run from the same venv where ait-bsc is installed (mitigated by the process-name filter, but pip can shell into python entrypoints)
Suppression filter
| where not (DstIpAddr in ("<known_ground_station_ip_1>","<known_ground_station_ip_2>")) and not (DstPortNumber in (8080, 8443) and BscCommandLine has "--allow-public-relay")
Response runbook
Triage: pull bsc.yaml from the host and confirm the destination IP+port is NOT in the configured handler list — any unrecognised loc is high-fidelity evil. Capture the BSC handler stats endpoint output (`GET /stats`) to enumerate every currently registered logger and their loc/port/path. Contain: stop the ait-bsc service and revoke any open TCP socket — note the advisory warns of an infinite-loop write bug on close, so plan disk-space monitoring during teardown. Hunt: search DeviceFileEvents for writes by the same ait-bsc PID within the same window, especially to .py / .sh / authorized_keys / cron paths; verify all AIT-Core site-packages files match the wheel hash; pivot the remote IP across DNS / proxy logs to find other internal hosts that reached out to it.

Securing CI/CD in an agentic world: Claude Code Github action case

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-06-05 7 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified a prompt injection pathway in Claude Code GitHub Action that allowed access to workflow secrets under specific conditions. This research examines the attack chain, responsible disclosure process, Anthropic's mitigation, and guidance for securing AI-powered CI/CD workflows. The post Securing CI/CD in an agentic world: Claude Code Github action case appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner · [LLM] Claude Code Read tool steered to cloud-credential files on GitHub Actions runner · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GitHub Actions runner: node from Claude Code Action egresses to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub endpoint
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Claude Code Action Read tool exfil: node opens /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux CI runner AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact exploitation primitive Microsoft Threat Intelligence described: the Claude Code Action's in-process Read tool, when steered by an injected prompt, opens /proc/self/environ (or /proc/<pid>/environ) to harvest the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, and OIDC credentials. Pre-fix (claude-code-action <2.1.128) the Bubblewrap sandbox + CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB does not cover Read, so the node process serving Claude Code opens /proc directly — a path almost nothing legitimate touches on a build runner. Rationale: Article names the exact primitive: 'eventually authorized to access /proc/self/environ, reading the workflow's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'. We pin on the Linux file path regex + node as the actor. The Read tool runs in-process inside node (not via Bash), so the file event is the only signal — there is no child process to pivot on. Corroborated by Flatt Security (flatt.tech) and Hacker News reporting which describe the same /proc/self/environ exfil chain. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/claude-code-github-action-flaw-let-one.html • https://oddguan.com/blog/comment-and-control-prompt-injection-credential-theft-claude-code-gemini-cli-github-copilot/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1212 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Container/process observability agents (datadog-agent, sysdig, falcon-sensor, osquery) using a bundled node helper to enumerate process env for inventory
  • Self-hosted runner image pre-flight scripts that introspect node's own environment for diagnostics (e.g. Node's --inspect tooling)
  • node-based Kubernetes operators (kube-state-metrics ports, Pulumi/CDK preview scripts) iterating /proc to map sibling containers
  • Security tooling that legitimately scans /proc for secret leakage (gitleaks/trufflehog wrapper jobs)
  • Node debugger sessions where a developer manually reads /proc/self/environ to diagnose env-var passing
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("datadog-agent", "sysdig", "falcon-sensor", "osqueryd", "trufflehog", "gitleaks")) and not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/opt/datadog-agent" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/opt/sysdig")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and folder path — confirm node was launched from `_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action*` or `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`. Pull the GitHub run ID from the runner work dir (`/home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>` or env GITHUB_RUN_ID) and fetch the triggering issue/PR body via gh api; look for HTML-comment payloads, /proc references, or Read-tool instructions. Step 2 (contain): Rotate ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN scopes, any OIDC-issued cloud creds, and every other secret exposed to that job. Disable the workflow file until upgraded to claude-code-action ≥2.1.128. For self-hosted runners, isolate the runner host pending forensics. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the same node PID to DeviceNetworkEvents/NetworkConnectIP4 in the surrounding 60s for outbound to non-Anthropic/non-GitHub IPs (exfil destination). Hunt repo-wide for other workflows pinning vulnerable claude-code-action SHAs. Audit recent PRs opened by the AI bot accoun

| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"^/proc/(self|\d+)/environ$"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("_work/", "actions-runner", "_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action", "runners/") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "claude-code-action")
